title: High-Throughput Library Pooling for NGS
author: Madeline Y Mayday
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tcdeis6

steps.title: Prepare Echo source plate
steps.instruction: Transfer the libraries into a new 384‑well Echo source plate; skip this step if the samples are already prepared. Dilute any samples as needed so that each well contains 22–25 µL total volume and at least 20 µL dead volume for accurate Echo dispensing.

steps.title: Sequence pool on low‑throughput instrument
steps.instruction: Run the pooled libraries on an Illumina iSeq (or any low‑throughput sequencer) to obtain the read count for each library.

steps.title: Calculate normalization factor
steps.instruction: From the iSeq output, compute the percent of reads for each library (x). Sum the inverse of each percent ( Σ 1/x ) to obtain the normalization factor N, which will be used to calculate pooling volumes. Required inputs: (1) percent of reads per library (x) and (2) desired total pool volume for submission (T µL).

steps.title: Determine per‑sample pooling volumes
steps.instruction: Use the normalization factor to calculate the volume of each library to add to the final pool so that the combined volume equals the desired total volume T (µL).

steps.title: Dispense libraries with Echo
steps.instruction: Using the Labcyte Echo, dispense the calculated volumes of each library from the source plate into a new 384‑well (or 96‑well) PCR destination plate. Observe the maximum working volume per well: for a 384‑well plate do not exceed 11 µL total per well. (If performing equal‑volume pooling, dispense 0.5 µL of each library per well; for 22 libraries this equals 12 µL, which is within the 12 µL limit for a 384‑well plate.)

steps.title: Combine wells into single tube
steps.instruction: Manually pool the contents of all destination wells into one Lo‑Bind DNA tube and mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Submit equimolar pool for sequencing
steps.instruction: The equimolar library pool is now ready for sequencing on a high‑throughput platform such as Illumina HiSeq or NovaSeq.
